open_headline: The world has its first trillionaire.
meet_red: I'm the poorest man in this world.
meet_blue_call_3: Click me. I'm the important one.
meet_blue: I'm the richest man in this world.
meet_tip: Click, press a key, or scroll to go on.
merit_1r: I work two shifts to pay the bills.
merit_2r: I'm smart too. / I have a PhD in physics.
merit_3b: I take big risks, and win big.
merit_3r: I take risks too. / But nobody catches me when I fall.
invite_2: I don't play games. / I build things.
invite_3: Just try it. We start equal.
invite_4: Equal? / Why would I give up my wealth?
invite_6: Fine. / I like a good experiment.
equal_ask: Give him some of my coins.
equal_give: Give one of {name}'s coins to {other}. {name} has {count}.
equal_over_r: Tempting. But give him one back.
r1_rules: The rules are simple. / We each put half on the table.
r1_flip: We flip a coin. / Blue side, you win. / Red side, I win.
r2_wait: Wait! / I have 4. I can't put in as much as you.
r2_half: Put in half of what you have.
r2_rule: So we always put in half / of what the poorer one has.
r2_why: Yes. That way everybody can keep playing.
r2_go: Smart. / Okay, let's go. / I'll win it back.
dare_ahead: Back where I started. / Well, I'm a bit ahead. Naturally.
dare_edge: Nobody has an edge. / Same odds, same rule. / Nobody gets rich.
dare_luck: That being rich means nothing. / No talent, no hard work. Just luck.
dare_bet: I'll bet half my wealth you can't.
dare_sure: You're either very sure / or very foolish.
dare_more: We need more players. / And many more rounds.
more_shapes: Different colours. Different shapes. / Only the size counts. The size is the wealth.
more_random: Each time, / two people are picked at random.
more_rule: They bet half of what the poorer one has. / Flip. The winner takes it all.
more_real: Real life is / much more complicated than this.
more_joke: Of course it is. / Want to hear a joke?
cow_offer: A joke about a cow, and why this model is so simple
cow_once: Once upon a time, / a farmer's cow stopped giving milk.
cow_0b: A biologist, a chemist, and a physicist.
cow_7b: The sphere alone answered this question. / Not every question. This one.
cow_frame_mine: And this game is my spherical cow. Simple on purpose.
cow_frame_next: Want to see how a person becomes a circle?
human_offer: How a person becomes a circle
human_1: I am not going to explain how he got rich.
guess_ask: Now it's your turn to guess.
guess_what: What do you think will happen?
guess_choice_3: A split: some rich, some poor
guess_choice_4: One giant, the rest near nothing
guess_stake: And how much would you bet on that?
guess_coffee: A coffee. Careful with your money. I respect that.
guess_lunch: A lunch. Fair. The winner picks the place.
guess_percent: One percent. Careful. That's how it starts.
card_rule_2: Each puts in {stake} of what the poorer one has.
card_rule_3: Flip a coin. The winner takes both.
run_go: Here we go. / Fair trades, one after another.
log_run: After {trades} trades, one of them holds {share} of everything.
run_blue_r: Run it again and see if your talent comes along.
run_red_r: Look at that. Am I a genius now?
why_after: The paper found the reason after the result. / The coin never saw a thing.
why_again: New winner. New reason. / The paper never prints "chance."
why_once: And that's one run. It shows, it doesn't prove. / The proof comes later.
sort_ask: A hundred people. / Too many to read at a glance.
sort_real: Most have almost nothing. A few have a lot. / That's just real life.
sort_edge: It's also this room. / And here, nobody had an edge.
sort_squeeze: This chart is useless, though. / Everyone is squeezed into one corner.
sort_times: Now each step means ten times more, / not ten more.
sort_even: One, ten, a hundred, a thousand. / Even steps. Huh.
sort_dust: Less than a cent goes in the dust box. / Zero has no place on this ruler.
sort_back: That's a histogram. / Back to the room?
card_histogram_1: Sort everyone into piles by how much they have.
card_histogram_2: A pile's height is how many people are in it.
card_histogram_3: A multiplying ruler shows what an ordinary one squeezes into a corner.
gini_ask: Economists love a single number. / What's ours?
gini_add: Now walk along the line / and add up their money as you go.
gini_equal: If everyone had the same, / the total would climb this straight line.
gini_gap: The gap between them is the Gini. / Zero: all the same. One: a single owner.
gini_toy: Want to see the equal case / and play with it?
card_gini_1: Line everyone up, poorest first, and add up their money as you go.
card_gini_2: 0: everyone has the same. 1: one owner, nothing for the rest.
eff_ask: A hundred players. / That's a lot of competition.
eff_equal: If all hundred had the same, / all hundred would count.
eff_brutal: This game is brutal. / No money, and you don't count at all. {count} left.
eff_give: Now give his money to one other person. / {count}. A bit less.
eff_half: Half of them own it all, equally? / {count}.
eff_try: Your turn. Four of them, four coins each. / Move the coins.
participation_formula: Open the black box: write each person's share of the room as sᵢ. Square the shares, add them, then take the reciprocal: 1 / Σsᵢ². This is the inverse Herfindahl concentration index.
card_participants_1: How many equal fortunes would be just as concentrated as this room.
card_participants_2: Everyone equal: all of them. One owner: 1. No money: you don't count.
turn_busy: At least it's a busy economy. / {trades} trades!
turn_count: Count the money that actually changes hands.
turn_start: At first, {early} of the room changed hands every round.
turn_now: By the end, {late}. / The trades go on. The money barely moves.
turn_dead: A dead economy. / Even I don't like that.
card_turnover_1: How much of all the money changes hands in one round: one trade per person.
card_turnover_2: A busy room moves a lot of its money. A concentrated one barely moves any, however many trades it makes.
end_one: That was one run. / It shows. It doesn't prove.
end_proof: The math says more. / Keep playing forever, and one person ends up with everything.
end_limit: Never on a date. It's a limit. / At any moment, it can still wobble.
end_longer: Want to see it run longer?
card_limit_1: Keep playing forever: with probability one, one person ends up with everything.
card_limit_2: A limit, not a date. At any moment the room can still wobble.
dial_ask: Your turn. / Pick a stake, from nothing to everything.
dial_zero: Zero: nothing moves. / That's no game at all.
dial_all: Everything on the table: / one loss and you're out. The richest holds {share}.
dial_same: {stake}: the stake you watched. / The richest holds {share}.
dial_law: Every stake above zero ends the same way. / The stake changes the journey, not the end.
card_stake_1: How much of the poorer one's money goes on each toss.
card_stake_2: Any stake above zero ends the same way. Smaller only takes longer. Zero is no game.
stop_ask: Enough watching. / Keep at least twenty players in the game.
stop_how: Tap a big fortune: a quarter goes into a pool / and comes back to everyone, equally.
stop_won: Thirty seconds, and still {count} players. / Your hand did it.
stop_lost: It closed after {seconds} seconds. / {taps} taps weren't enough.
stop_hand: Notice what your hand did: / watch, pick one, react. Again and again.
stop_rule: Next, not a hand. A rule. / Nobody gets picked.
levy_ask: Your hand gets tired. / A rule doesn't.
levy_collect: Once a round, the same share from everyone: / a quarter.
levy_same: Everyone lost a quarter. / Nothing changed.
levy_shares: Right. Everyone shrank the same. / The shares didn't move.
levy_return: Now the pool goes back, / in equal parts.
levy_net: The average broke even. / Below it, more came back. Above it, less.
levy_kept: And the room kept every coin.
card_levy_1: Once a round: the same share of every fortune into one pool.
card_levy_2: The pool comes back in equal parts.
card_levy_3: Below the average gains, the average breaks even, above it pays in. Nothing is lost.
match_ask: Now let it trade. Same luck, twice: / one room without the rule, one with it.
match_result: Without the rule: about {a} players. / With it: about {b}.
match_right: Trades, and a 3% levy shared back
match_same: Every toss the same. / Only the rule changed.
map_ask: One pair is confusing. / Which settings keep the room open?
map_all: Try them all: stake across, levy up. / Each square, how many still count.
map_fit: A small levy can hold a big stake: / double the stake, about four times the levy.
verdict_1: The coin was fair the whole time. It never saw a name.
verdict_2: Then how did one of us end up with everything?
verdict_3: Money didn't buy better odds. It bought more tosses you could survive.
verdict_4: Then a shared levy with an equal return kept more people able to play.
verdict_6: No. I'm worried about the field merit plays on.
verdict_7: If merit is supposed to win…
verdict_8: …keep the game open long enough for merit to play.
sandbox_2: The machine is yours. Break our argument.
